# Introduction

This report analyzes long-term ecosystem dynamics at LTER Site 1 in Moorea, French Polynesia. We examine relationships between benthic community composition, environmental conditions, fish assemblages, and ecosystem metabolism over nearly two decades (2005-2025). The analysis integrates multiple datasets to understand how coral reef ecosystems are responding to environmental change.

```{r setup}
#| cache: false
```

# Data

## 1. Temperature Data

Extract yearly average and maximum daily temperature values from the backreef temperature time series.

```{r temperature-processing}
#| label: process-temperature

# Read and process temperature data
Temp_LTER1 <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "MCR_LTER02_BTM_Backreef_Forereef_20251114.csv")) |>
  filter(reef_type_code == "Backreef")

# Calculate daily means, then yearly statistics (optimized with single pass)
Mean_year_Temp <- Temp_LTER1 |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time_local)) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(daily_temp = mean(temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Year = year(date)) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    Mean_temp = mean(daily_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max_temp = max(daily_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Save processed data
write_csv(Mean_year_Temp, here("Data", "InSituTemp.csv"))

# Quick summary
summary(Mean_year_Temp)
```

## 2. Nutrient Data

Process macroalgae tissue nitrogen content and water column nutrients, using tissue N to impute missing water column data.

```{r nutrient-processing}
#| label: process-nutrients

# Turbinaria %N data (tissue nitrogen as nutrient proxy)
Turb <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "MCR_LTER_Macroalgal_CHN_2005_to_2024_20250616.csv")) |>
  filter(
    Habitat == "Backreef",
    Genus == "Turbinaria",
    Site == "LTER_1",
    !is.na(N)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    N_percent = mean(N, na.rm = TRUE),
    C_percent = mean(C, na.rm = TRUE),
    CN = mean(CN_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(Turb, here("Data", "Turb_mean.csv"))

# Water column nutrients (bimonthly surveys 2005-2018)
water <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "WaterColumnN.csv")) |>
  mutate(
    Date = mdy(Date),
    Year = year(Date)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(across(Phosphate:Nitrite_and_Nitrate,  \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Site = "LTER 1")

write_csv(water, here("Data", "Water_N_mean.csv"))

# Impute water N+N from tissue N using linear model
AllNutrients <- Turb |>
  full_join(water, by = "Year") |>
  arrange(Year)

# Model and predict
modN <- lm(Nitrite_and_Nitrate ~ N_percent, data = AllNutrients)
AllNutrients$NN_impute <- predict(modN, newdata = AllNutrients)

# Model summary
cat("\nNutrient imputation model (Nitrite+Nitrate ~ Tissue %N):\n")
summary(modN)

cat("\nNutrient correlation values (Nitrite+Nitrate ~ Tissue %N):\n")
AllNutrients2<-AllNutrients %>% drop_na()
corTest(x=AllNutrients2$Nitrite_and_Nitrate, y=AllNutrients2$N_percent)
```

## 3. Benthic Cover Data

Calculate percent cover for functional groups from benthic transect surveys.

```{r benthic-processing}
#| label: process-benthic

# Read and classify benthic data
BenthicCover_Algae <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "MCR_LTER_Annual_Survey_Benthic_Cover_20251009.csv")) |>
  filter(Habitat == "Backreef")

# Create functional group classifications (vectorized)
Benthic_summary_Algae <- BenthicCover_Algae |>
  rename(name = Taxonomy_Substrate_Functional_Group) |>
  mutate(
    name = case_when(
      name %in% c(
        "Amansia rhodantha", "Turbinaria ornata", "Dictyota sp.", "Halimeda sp.",
        "Galaxaura sp.", "Liagora ceranoides", "Cyanophyta", "Halimeda minima",
        "Amphiroa fragilissima", "Caulerpa serrulata", "Corallimorpharia",
        "Dictyota friabilis", "Galaxaura rugosa", "Cladophoropsis membranacea",
        "Galaxaura filamentosa", "Halimeda discoidea", "Peyssonnelia inamoena",
        "Caulerpa racemosa", "Valonia ventricosa", "Actinotrichia fragilis",
        "Dictyota bartayresiana", "Microdictyon umbilicatum", "Halimeda distorta",
        "Halimeda incrassata", "Halimeda macroloba", "Dictyota implexa",
        "Gelidiella acerosa", "Dictyosphaeria cavernosa", "Valonia aegagropila",
        "Microdictyon okamurae", "Halimeda opuntia", "Dichotomaria obtusata",
        "Chlorodesmis fastigiata", "Phyllodictyon anastomosans", "Phormidium sp.",
        "Cladophoropsis luxurians", "Sargassum pacificum", "Chnoospora implexa",
        "Halimeda taenicola", "Boodlea kaeneana", "Padina boryana",
        "Coelothrix irregularis", "Gelidiella sp.", "Hydroclathrus clathratus",
        "Dictyota divaricata", "Hypnea spinella", "Dichotomaria marginata",
        "Sporolithon sp.", "Chaetomorpha antennina", "Asparagopsis taxiformis"
      ) ~ "Fleshy Macroalgae",
      name %in% c(
        "Algal Turf", "Damselfish Turf", "Coral Rubble",
        "Lobophora variegata", "Shell Debris", "Bare Space"
      ) ~ "Turf/Cyanobacteria",
      name %in% c(
        "Peyssonnelia bornetii", "Peyssonnelia sp.",
        "Sponge", "Tridacna sp.", "No data"
      ) ~ "Sand",
      TRUE ~ name
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, Site, name) |>
  summarise(
    total_cover = sum(Percent_Cover, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_cover = 100 * total_cover / 5000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(Site = str_replace_all(Site, "_", " "))

write_csv(Benthic_summary_Algae, here("Data", "Benthic_summary_algae.csv"))

# Calculate total calcifiers and living cover
Total_Calc <- Benthic_summary_Algae |>
  filter(name %in% c("Coral", "Crustose Corallines")) |>
  group_by(Year, Site) |>
  reframe(total_Calc = sum(mean_cover))

TotalLiving <- Benthic_summary_Algae |>
  filter(name %in% c("Coral", "Crustose Corallines", "Fleshy Macroalgae")) |>
  group_by(Year, Site) |>
  summarise(
    mean_alive = sum(mean_cover),
    mean_fleshy = sum(mean_cover[name == "Fleshy Macroalgae"], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_coral = sum(mean_cover[name == "Coral"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## 4. Fish Biomass Data

Process fish survey data by trophic groups.

```{r fish-processing}
#| label: process-fish

# Read and process fish data
fish <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "MCR_LTER_Annual_Fish_Survey_20260304.csv"))

# Process by trophic groups (optimized filtering)
fish_summary <- fish |>
  filter(
    Site == "LTER_1",
    Habitat == "Backreef",
    Biomass < 8000, # Remove outlier sharks
    Biomass >= 0 # Remove negative (missing) values
  ) |>
  mutate(
    trophic_new = case_when(
      Fine_Trophic %in% c("Brusher", "Browser", "Excavator", "Scraper") ~ "Herbivores",
      Fine_Trophic == "Corallivore" ~ "Corallivore",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, trophic_new) |>
  summarise(
    fish_g_m2 = sum(Biomass, na.rm = TRUE) / 1200, # 4 transects × 300 m²
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(fish_summary, here("Data", "fish_summary.csv"))
```

## 5. Primary Production Processing

Process raw production data and extract Pmax and Rd using Bayesian photosynthesis-irradiance curves.

```{r pp-processing}
#| label: process-pp
#| cache: true

# Read all QC PP files efficiently
filedir <- here("Data", "raw_data", "QC_PP")
files <- dir(path = filedir, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)

All_PP_data <- files |>
  set_names() |>
  map_df(read_csv, .id = "filename", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(DateTime = mdy_hm(DateTime))

# Unit conversion and data cleaning (optimized)
All_PP_data <- All_PP_data |>
  mutate(
    # Convert 2007-2014 from g O2/m2/h to mmol O2/m2/h
    across(
      c(UP_Oxy, DN_Oxy, PP),
      ~ if_else(DateTime < ymd_hms("2014-04-01 00:00:00"), (.x / 32) * 1000, .x)
    ),
    Date = as_date(DateTime),
    DielDateTime = DateTime + hours(12),
    DielDate = as_date(DielDateTime),
    Year = year(DateTime)
  ) |>
  filter(!Date %in% mdy(c("5/27/2011", "5/28/2011", "1/21/2014", "05/25/2024")))

# Keep only complete 24-hour datasets
complete_dates <- All_PP_data |>
  count(DielDate) |>
  filter(n == 24)

All_PP_data <- complete_dates |>
  left_join(All_PP_data, by = "DielDate")

# Calculate GP and environmental averages
Daily_R <- All_PP_data |>
  group_by(Year, Season, DielDate) |>
  summarise(R_average = mean(PP[PAR == 0], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

All_PP_data <- All_PP_data |>
  left_join(Daily_R, by = c("Year", "Season", "DielDate")) |>
  mutate(
    GP = if_else(PAR == 0, NA_real_, PP - R_average),
    GP = if_else(GP < 0, NA_real_, GP),
    Temperature_mean = (UP_Temp + DN_Temp) / 2,
    Flow_mean = (UP_Velocity_mps + DN_Velocity_mps) / 2
  )

# Calculate yearly averages
Year_Averages_PP <- All_PP_data |>
  mutate(
    NP = PP,
    R = if_else(PP < 0, PP, NA_real_)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    NP_mean = mean(NP, na.rm = TRUE),
    NP_SE = sd(NP, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    NP_max = max(NP, na.rm = TRUE),
    GP_mean = mean(GP, na.rm = TRUE),
    GP_SE = sd(GP, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    R_mean = mean(R, na.rm = TRUE),
    R_SE = sd(R, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    Temperature_mean = mean(Temperature_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    Flow_mean = mean(Flow_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    PAR_mean = mean(PAR[PAR > 0], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Bayesian Photosynthesis-Irradiance (PI) Curve Analysis

We fit a Bayesian non-linear model to extract photosynthetic parameters (alpha, Pmax, and Rd) for each year. The model uses a rectangular hyperbola:

$$PP = \frac{\alpha \cdot P_{max} \cdot PAR}{\alpha \cdot PAR + P_{max}} + R_d$$

where: - $\alpha$ = initial slope (photosynthetic efficiency) - $P_{max}$ = maximum photosynthetic capacity - $R_d$ = dark respiration (ecosystem respiration) - $PAR$ = photosynthetically active radiation

```{r bayesian-pi-curve}
# Bayesian PI curves to extract light-independent Pmax and Rd
LTER1_Pnet <- All_PP_data |>
  mutate(
    tempc = Temperature_mean,
    Flowmean = Flow_mean,
    flow_log = log(Flowmean),
    UPDN = as.factor(UPDN),
    Year = as.factor(Year)
  )

# Fit Bayesian nonlinear model
fit1_f <- brm(
  bf(
    PP ~ ((alpha * Pmax * PAR) / (alpha * PAR + Pmax)) + Rd,
    nl = TRUE,
    alpha ~ 0 + Year,
    Pmax ~ 0 + Year,
    Rd ~ 0 + Year
  ) + student(),
  data = LTER1_Pnet,
  set_rescor(FALSE),
  prior = c(
    prior(normal(0.1, 10), nlpar = "alpha", lb = 0),
    prior(normal(-100, 10), nlpar = "Rd", ub = 0),
    prior(normal(100, 10), nlpar = "Pmax", lb = 0)
  ),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 20),
  cores = 3,
  chains = 3,
  seed = 223,
  iter = 8000,
  warmup = 2000
)

# Extract Pmax and Rd coefficients
names <- rownames(fixef(fit1_f))
coefficients <- as_tibble(fixef(fit1_f)) |>
  mutate(params = names)

PRValues <- coefficients |>
  separate(params, sep = "_", into = c("param_type", "yearname"), remove = FALSE) |>
  filter(param_type %in% c("Pmax", "Rd")) |>
  separate(yearname, sep = "r", into = c("y", "year")) |>
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year)) |>
  select(Year = year, Estimate, param_type) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = param_type, values_from = Estimate)

# Combine with raw averages
Year_Averages_PP <- Year_Averages_PP |>
  full_join(PRValues, by = "Year") |>
  mutate(Rd = -Rd) # Make Rd positive

# Calculate Bayesian R²
pi_curve_r2 <- median(bayes_R2(fit1_f)[, 1])
cat(sprintf("\nPhotosynthesis-Irradiance Curve Model:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Bayesian R²: %.3f\n", pi_curve_r2))
cat(sprintf("  This indicates the model explains %.1f%% of variance in net production\n", pi_curve_r2 * 100))

write_csv(Year_Averages_PP, here("Data", "Year_Averages_PP.csv"))
```

```{r integrate-data}

# Read processed data files
Year_Averages_PP <- read_csv(here("Data", "Year_Averages_PP.csv"))
Turb <- read_csv(here("Data", "Turb_mean.csv"))
water <- read_csv(here("Data", "Water_N_mean.csv"))

  pivot_wider(names_from = trophic_new, values_from = fish_g_m2) |>

Benthic_summary_Algae <- read_csv(here("Data", "Benthic_summary_algae.csv"))

# Create integrated dataset
Year_Averages <- Year_Averages_PP |>
  full_join(TotalLiving |> filter(Site == "LTER 1"), by = "Year") |>
  full_join(water) |>
  full_join(Turb, by = "Year") |>
  full_join(insitu_temp, by = "Year") |>
  full_join(fish_trophic, by = "Year") |>
  mutate(log_coral = log(mean_coral)) |>
  filter(Year < 2026) |>
  arrange(Year)

# Display structure
glimpse(Year_Averages)
```

# Methods

## Photosynthesis-Irradiance Curve Analysis

Annual values of maximum photosynthetic capacity (Pmax) and ecosystem respiration (Rd) were extracted from a Bayesian nonlinear model fit to 2,928 net O₂ flux measurements using the **brms** package (Bürkner 2017) and Stan (Carpenter et al. 2017). We used the rectangular hyperbola:

$$\mathrm{PP} = \frac{\alpha \cdot P_{\max} \cdot \mathrm{PAR}}{\alpha \cdot \mathrm{PAR} + P_{\max}} + R_d$$

where PP is net community production, PAR is photosynthetically active radiation, and α is photosynthetic efficiency. Year-specific parameters (α, Pmax, Rd) were estimated simultaneously from all deployments. A Student-*t* likelihood accommodated measurement outliers. Priors were weakly informative: α ~ Normal$_+$(0.1, 10); Pmax ~ Normal$_+$(100, 10); Rd ~ Normal$_-$(−100, 10). Three chains ran for 8,000 iterations (2,000 warmup) at adapt_delta = 0.95. Posterior Rd values were multiplied by −1 to express ecosystem respiration as positive rates.

## Temporal Trend Analysis

We estimated standardised temporal trends for 10 ecosystem variables (coral cover, fleshy macroalgae, corallivore biomass, herbivore biomass, algal nitrogen content, ecosystem respiration, Pmax, net ecosystem production, maximum temperature, nitrate+nitrite) using independent Bayesian linear regression models (Variable ~ Year, default **brms** priors) on z-scored data. The slope posterior (change per standardised year) was used to assess direction and magnitude of each trend. Effects were considered directional when the 95% credible interval excluded zero. Bayesian R² (Gelman et al. 2019) is reported as the posterior median. Absolute percent change was calculated between the first and last non-missing observations on the original scale.

## Correlation Analysis

Pearson correlations among all major ecosystem variables were computed and visualised as a mixed correlation matrix (upper triangle: ellipses scaled by correlation strength; lower triangle: numeric values; diagonal: variable names). Significance was assessed using two-tailed t-tests; variables were ordered by hierarchical clustering of the correlation matrix.

## Structural Equation Modeling

To evaluate simultaneous causal pathways among ecosystem components, we fit a Bayesian multivariate SEM in **brms** with residual correlations disabled (`set_rescor = FALSE`). The directed acyclic graph (DAG) was motivated by ecological theory and temporal precedence, comprising eight response equations:

| # | Equation |
|---|----------|
| 1 | Temperature ~ Year |
| 2 | log(coral cover) \| trunc(ub = 3.39) ~ temperature + yearresid |
| 3 | log(ecosystem respiration) ~ log(coral cover) + temperature |
| 4 | log(fleshy macroalgae) \| trunc(ub = 2.26) ~ log(coral cover) |
| 5 | log(Pmax) ~ log(coral cover) + temperature + log(ecosystem respiration) |
| 6 | corallivore biomass ~ log(coral cover) |
| 7 | herbivore biomass ~ log(fleshy macroalgae) |
| 8 | log(nitrogen content) ~ log(ecosystem respiration) |

All continuous responses were log-transformed and z-score standardised before modelling. The `yearresid` predictor is the residual of calendar year regressed on maximum annual temperature. Because calendar year is correlated with many concurrent processes (e.g., the 2010 *Acanthaster* outbreak and subsequent dynamics, shifts in fishing pressure, ocean acidification, and any undetected observer or sampling effects), `yearresid` represents an unresolved bundle of secular non-thermal pressures operating over 2005–2025 and cannot be attributed to any single mechanism. Cover responses were upper-truncated at the z-log scale equivalent of 100% cover to respect the biological ceiling; truncation values (3.39 for coral, 2.26 for fleshy algae) were verified to back-transform to exactly 100%.

Missing predictor values (ecosystem respiration and temperature as predictors of Pmax; ecosystem respiration as predictor of N content) were handled via **brms** integrated missing-data imputation (`mi()` syntax). Priors were weakly informative: regression coefficients ~ Normal(0, 2); intercepts ~ Normal(0, 2); residual SDs ~ Normal$_+$(0, 0.25) for the temperature sub-model and Normal$_+$(0, 2) otherwise.

### Temporal autocorrelation in the coral sub-model

Preliminary inspection of coral cover residuals from a baseline regression showed pronounced positive temporal autocorrelation (lag-1 Pearson *r* = 0.74; Durbin–Watson statistic ≈ 0.51), indicating that standard independent-errors assumptions would produce credible intervals that are too narrow for the coral equation. This pattern is ecologically interpretable: annual disturbances (bleaching, storms) have a half-life of roughly 8–9 years before decaying to half their original amplitude, consistent with the slow recovery dynamics known for Indo-Pacific reef systems. To address this, the coral sub-model included a first-order autoregressive residual structure, specified as `ar(time = Year, p = 1)` within the **brms** formula. The AR(1) coefficient φ received a weakly informative Normal(0, 0.5) prior (the default in **brms**); all structural regression coefficients retained Normal(0, 2) priors. AR(1) was applied only to the coral sub-model because coral cover residuals showed the strongest temporal dependence; other residual series were inspected but showed weaker patterns not requiring correction. Three chains ran for 10,000 iterations (5,000 warmup) with adapt_delta = 0.99 and max_treedepth = 15. Convergence was assessed via Rhat (< 1.01 for all parameters), bulk and tail effective sample sizes (> 1,000), and posterior predictive checks.

### Parsimonious (reduced) SEM

A reduced model was fit by removing three pathways whose 95% credible intervals included zero in the full model: Temperature → Respiration (direct), Temperature → Pmax (direct), and Coral → Pmax (direct). All retained coefficients were stable between full and reduced models (within 0.05 SD). The reduced model, with AR(1) on the coral sub-model, is used for all ecosystem projections. The AR(1) correction widens credible intervals on the coral path coefficients while leaving medians essentially unchanged; all directional conclusions from the full model are preserved. For projections, only the structural regression coefficients (not the AR residual term) are propagated forward: the AR term corrects for non-independence in the fitted period but cannot be extrapolated as a future forcing. Consequently, projection uncertainty is governed entirely by the posterior distributions of the structural path coefficients, which now correctly reflect the effective sample size of the coral time series.

### Direct and indirect temperature effects

Total standardised effects of temperature on each ecosystem variable were decomposed into direct paths and indirect paths (products of coefficients along each chain through the DAG) using all 15,000 post-warmup draws. Indirect effects were computed as the product of relevant path coefficients; for example, the indirect effect on respiration was β(Temp→Coral) × β(Coral→Rd). Total effects are the sum across all contributing paths. An effect was considered credible if its 95% CI excluded zero.

## Ecosystem Projections

### CMIP6 climate scenario projections (to 2100)

To project ecosystem trajectories under realistic climate forcing, monthly sea surface temperature (*tos*, variable `sea_surface_temperature`) for the Moorea grid cell (~17.5°S, 149.8°W) was obtained from five coupled CMIP6 ScenarioMIP models — ACCESS-CM2 (Bi et al. 2020), IPSL-CM6A-LR (Boucher et al. 2020), MIROC6 (Tatebe et al. 2019), MPI-ESM1-2-LR (Müller et al. 2018), and UKESM1-0-LL (Sellar et al. 2019) (Eyring et al. 2016) — downloaded from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (`projections-cmip6` dataset; Copernicus Climate Change Service 2023; https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/projections-cmip6; DOI: 10.24381/cds.c866074c) via the **ecmwfr** R package (Hufkens et al. 2019; https://bluegreen-labs.github.io/ecmwfr/). These five models were selected as the subset of originally targeted CMIP6 models that provide `sea_surface_temperature` data for both the historical experiment (1950–2014) and all three SSP scenarios (2015–2100) in the CDS dataset. Data were requested under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways: SSP1-2.6 (strong mitigation, ~1.5–2°C global warming by 2100), SSP2-4.5 (intermediate stabilisation), and SSP5-8.5 (high emissions, ~4–5°C warming; O'Neill et al. 2016; Riahi et al. 2017). Historical and SSP series were stitched at 2015. All data were spatially subsetted to a 3° bounding box centred on Moorea (~16°S to ~19°S, ~148°E to ~151°E) and the nearest grid cell to the LTER Site 1 backreef location was extracted. Monthly *tos* values were converted from Kelvin to Celsius where necessary, aggregated to annual maxima per model-year.

Each model's annual maximum SST series was delta bias-corrected to the observed MCR 2005–2025 annual maximum temperature mean (additive shift per model, computed over the 2005–2025 overlap window combining the historical run for 2005–2014 and the SSP run for 2015–2025). Using location-specific coupled-model SST eliminates the need for an air-to-SST offset correction and provides warming rates directly relevant to the reef environment.

Uncertainty sources from CMIP6 climate models and from the SEM are handled separately to remain interpretable. For the **Temperature panel**, the ensemble p10–p90 range across the five bias-corrected models is shown directly as the uncertainty ribbon — this reflects purely inter-model structural uncertainty in future warming. For the **ecological variable panels**, a single deterministic ensemble-median temperature trajectory is propagated through all 3,000 Bayesian SEM posterior draws. Because all draws use identical temperature inputs, the resulting 95% credible interval reflects SEM path-coefficient uncertainty only (parameter uncertainty), not climate-model structural uncertainty. The non-temperature predictor (*yearresid* — residual of calendar year after removing the temperature trend, representing an unresolved bundle of secular non-thermal pressures) is held constant at its observed 2025 z-score for the entire projection period (2026–2100), so that all scenario-dependent divergence from 2026 onward is driven exclusively by CMIP6 temperature anomalies relative to the 2025 baseline. This assumption implies that the aggregate intensity of the non-thermal pressures captured by `yearresid` — including disturbance legacies such as the 2010 *Acanthaster* outbreak — remains at its end-of-record (2025) level indefinitely; it does not represent a neutral or average condition. The historical period (2005–2025) shows observed ecosystem values directly in all panels — lines connect the observed annual values and open circles mark individual observations — without SEM interpolation.

## Software and Reproducibility

Key packages: **tidyverse** 2.0 (Wickham et al. 2019), **brms** 2.21 (Bürkner 2017), **tidybayes** 3.0 (Kay 2023), **patchwork** 1.2 (Pedersen 2024), **ggraph** 2.1 and **igraph** 1.6 (Csárdi & Nepusz 2006), **httr2** (Wickham 2023), **zoo** (Zeileis & Grothendieck 2005), **cowplot** (Wilke 2024), **ecmwfr** (Hufkens et al. 2019; https://bluegreen-labs.github.io/ecmwfr/), **ncdf4** (Pierce 2024). Stan 2.32 served as the computational backend. CMIP6 SST data were accessed from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/projections-cmip6; DOI: 10.24381/cds.c866074c). All analysis code and processed data are available at \[**INSERT REPOSITORY DOI**\]; MCR LTER raw data are publicly archived through the EDI Data Portal (https://edirepository.org).

## Temporal Trends

Assess standardized change per year using Bayesian linear models.

```{r temporal-trends}
#| label: temporal-trends
#| cache: true

# Create standardized dataset
std_data <- Year_Averages |>
  select(
    mean_coral, mean_fleshy, Pmax, Rd, N_percent,
    Herbivores, Corallivore, NP_mean, Max_temp, GP_mean,
    Nitrite_and_Nitrate, Phosphate
  ) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)))) |>
  bind_cols(Year_Averages |> select(Year))

# Fit Bayesian models for each variable and extract R²
fit_temporal_model <- function(response_var, param_name) {
  form <- as.formula(paste(response_var, "~ Year"))
  mod <- brm(form, data = std_data, silent = 2, refresh = 0, seed = 223)
  
  # Extract posterior samples
  post <- as_tibble(as.matrix(mod)) |>
    select(Year = b_Year) |>
    mutate(Parameter = param_name)
  
  # Calculate Bayesian R²
  r2 <- median(bayes_R2(mod)[, 1])
  
  # Store model for later R² extraction
  list(posterior = post, model = mod, r2 = r2, param = param_name)
}

# Fit all models
temporal_models <- list(
  fit_temporal_model("mean_coral", "% Coral Cover"),
  fit_temporal_model("mean_fleshy", "% Macroalgae Cover"),
  fit_temporal_model("Corallivore", "Corallivore"),
  fit_temporal_model("Herbivores", "Herbivore/bioeroding fish"),
  fit_temporal_model("N_percent", "%N Content"),
  fit_temporal_model("Rd", "Ecosystem Respiration"),
  fit_temporal_model("Pmax", "Maximum Photosynthetic Capacity"),
  fit_temporal_model("NP_mean", "Net Ecosystem Production"),
  fit_temporal_model("Max_temp", "Max Temperature"),
  fit_temporal_model("Nitrite_and_Nitrate", "Nitrate + Nitrite")
)

# Extract posteriors for plotting
temporal_results <- temporal_models |>
  map_df(~.x$posterior)

# Print R² values
cat("\n=== Temporal Trend Model Performance (Bayesian R²) ===\n\n")
temporal_models |>
  map_df(~tibble(Parameter = .x$param, R2 = .x$r2)) |>
  arrange(desc(R2)) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r temporal-plot}
#| label: fig-temporal
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "**Six of ten ecosystem variables show credible directional change over 20 years, with coral cover, algal nitrogen, and nitrate declining while macroalgae and herbivore biomass increased.** (A) Posterior distributions of the standardised temporal slope (change per SD yr⁻¹) from independent Bayesian linear regression models fit to z-scored annual data (n = 13–20 annual observations per variable, 2005–2025, depending on availability). The vertical dashed line marks zero; white tick marks indicate 95% posterior credible intervals. Red = increasing trend, blue = decreasing trend; credible intervals excluding zero indicate directional change. (B) Raw annual observations (points) overlaid with posterior median trend lines and 95% credible interval ribbons on original measurement scales. Variables shown (top to bottom): coral cover (%), fleshy macroalgae cover (%), corallivore fish biomass (g m⁻²), herbivore fish biomass (g m⁻²), algal tissue nitrogen content (%), ecosystem respiration Rd (mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹), maximum photosynthetic capacity Pmax (mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹), net community production NP (mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹), annual maximum sea surface temperature (°C), and water-column nitrate + nitrite (µmol L⁻¹). Bayesian R² (posterior median) is shown for each trend model."

# Noto Sans has full Unicode coverage (superscripts, µ, °, subscripts)
# Falls back gracefully if offline — font is cached after first download

# ── Nature-ready base theme (10 pt, classic, no gridlines) ─────────────────
# Exported at 183 × 220 mm; base_size = 10 → 10 pt text at final print size.
theme_nature <- function(base_size = 10) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text             = element_text(family = "noto"),
      axis.text        = element_text(size = base_size, color = "black"),
      axis.title       = element_text(size = base_size),
      axis.line        = element_line(linewidth = 0.35, color = "black"),
      axis.ticks       = element_line(linewidth = 0.35, color = "black"),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text       = element_text(size = 10, face = "plain", color = "grey20"),
      panel.spacing    = unit(0.5, "lines"),
      legend.position  = "none",
      plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)
    )
}

col_inc <- "#E64B35"   # NPG red  — increasing
col_dec <- "#4DBBD5"   # NPG teal — decreasing

# ── Summarise posterior slopes (order + color mapping) ─────────────────────
slope_summary <- temporal_results |>
  group_by(Parameter) |>
  summarise(
    median_slope = median(Year),
    direction    = if_else(median_slope > 0, "Increasing", "Decreasing"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(median_slope)

param_levels <- slope_summary$Parameter

# ── Scale parameters — defined here so they are available to both panels ────
short_label_map <- tibble(
  var = c("mean_coral", "mean_fleshy", "Corallivore", "Herbivores",
          "N_percent", "Rd", "Pmax", "NP_mean", "Max_temp", "Nitrite_and_Nitrate"),
  Parameter = c("% Coral Cover", "% Macroalgae Cover", "Corallivore",
                "Herbivore/bioeroding fish", "%N Content", "Ecosystem Respiration",
                "Maximum Photosynthetic Capacity", "Net Ecosystem Production",
                "Max Temperature", "Nitrate + Nitrite"),
  label = c(
    "Coral cover\n(%)",
    "Macroalgae cover\n(%)",
    "Corallivore\n(g m\u207b\u00b2)",

    "N content\n(%)",
    "Respiration\n(mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 hr\u207b\u00b9)",
    "Pmax\n(mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 hr\u207b\u00b9)",
    "NEP\n(mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 hr\u207b\u00b9)",
    "Max temperature\n(\u00b0C)",
    "Nitrate+nitrite\n(\u00b5mol L\u207b\u00b9)"
  )
)

scale_params <- tibble(
  var = short_label_map$var,
  mu  = map_dbl(short_label_map$var, \(x) mean(Year_Averages[[x]], na.rm = TRUE)),
  sd  = map_dbl(short_label_map$var, \(x) sd(Year_Averages[[x]],   na.rm = TRUE))
) |>
  left_join(short_label_map, by = "var")

label_levels <- scale_params$label[match(param_levels, scale_params$Parameter)]

# Short names for panel a y-axis (strip units line from panel b labels)
short_name_map <- scale_params |>
  select(Parameter, label) |>
  mutate(short_name = str_remove(label, "\n.*"))

# ── Panel a: Posterior density ridges ──────────────────────────────────────
panel_a <- temporal_results |>
  left_join(slope_summary |> select(Parameter, direction), by = "Parameter") |>
  left_join(short_name_map, by = "Parameter") |>

    scale = 0.88, rel_min_height = 0.01
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increasing" = col_inc, "Decreasing" = col_dec)) +

  annotate("segment",
           x = 0.02, xend = 0.26, y = 0.38, yend = 0.38,

# ── Back-transform fitted values and raw data to original scales ────────────

# ── Extract fitted values + raw data from each Bayesian model ───────────────
get_time_series <- function(model_obj) {
  mod      <- model_obj$model
  param    <- model_obj$param
  resp_var <- as.character(formula(mod)$formula)[2]
  year_seq <- tibble(Year = seq(min(std_data$Year), max(std_data$Year), by = 0.5))
  fitted_df <- fitted(mod, newdata = year_seq) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    bind_cols(year_seq) |>
    mutate(Parameter = param)
  raw_df <- std_data |>
    select(Year, value = all_of(resp_var)) |>
    mutate(Parameter = param)
  list(fitted = fitted_df, raw = raw_df)
}

all_series <- map(temporal_models, get_time_series)

fitted_all <- map_df(all_series, ~.x$fitted) |>
  left_join(slope_summary |> select(Parameter, direction), by = "Parameter") |>
  left_join(scale_params |> select(Parameter, mu, sd, label), by = "Parameter") |>
  mutate(
    Estimate_orig = Estimate * sd + mu,
    Q2.5_orig     = Q2.5    * sd + mu,
    Q97.5_orig    = Q97.5   * sd + mu,
    label = factor(label, levels = label_levels)
  )

raw_all <- map_df(all_series, ~.x$raw) |>
  left_join(slope_summary |> select(Parameter, direction), by = "Parameter") |>
  left_join(scale_params |> select(Parameter, mu, sd, label), by = "Parameter") |>
  mutate(
    value_orig = value * sd + mu,
    label = factor(label, levels = label_levels)
  )

# ── Bayesian R² annotations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
r2_df <- map_df(temporal_models, ~tibble(Parameter = .x$param, r2 = .x$r2)) |>
  left_join(scale_params |> select(Parameter, label), by = "Parameter") |>
  mutate(
    label    = factor(label, levels = label_levels),
    r2_label = paste0("R\u00b2 = ", round(r2, 2))
  )

# ── Y-axis labels via expression(atop()) — reliable across all PDF fonts ─────
# ── Y-axis labels: single-line expressions ───────────────────────────────────
# Single-line keeps the rotated title height ≈ font size (~10 pt) vs two-line
# atop() which doubles it, causing excess gap between label and plot area.
yaxis_labels <- list(
  "% Coral Cover"                   = "Coral cover (%)",
  "% Macroalgae Cover"              = "Macroalgae (%)",
  "Corallivore"                     = expression("Corallivore (g m"^-2*")"),
  "Herbivore/bioeroding fish"       = expression("Herbivores (g m"^-2*")"),
  "%N Content"                      = "N content (%)",
  "Ecosystem Respiration"           = expression("Rd (mmol O"[2]*" m"^-2*" h"^-1*")"),
  "Maximum Photosynthetic Capacity" = expression("Pmax (mmol O"[2]*" m"^-2*" h"^-1*")"),
  "Net Ecosystem Production"        = expression("NEP (mmol O"[2]*" m"^-2*" h"^-1*")"),
  "Max Temperature"                 = "Max temp. (\u00b0C)",
  "Nitrate + Nitrite"               = expression("N+N (\u00b5mol L"^-1*")")
)

# ── Individual panels B–K ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# show_xticks: TRUE only for bottom row (J, K = positions 9–10)
make_ts_panel <- function(param_name, letter, show_xticks = FALSE) {
  fd <- fitted_all |> filter(Parameter == param_name)
  rd <- raw_all    |> filter(Parameter == param_name)
  r2 <- r2_df      |> filter(Parameter == param_name)

  ggplot() +
    geom_ribbon(data = fd,
      aes(x = Year, ymin = Q2.5_orig, ymax = Q97.5_orig, fill = direction),
      alpha = 0.18) +
    geom_line(data = fd,
      aes(x = Year, y = Estimate_orig, color = direction),
      linewidth = 0.55) +
    geom_point(data = rd, aes(x = Year, y = value_orig),
      size = 0.85, alpha = 0.70, shape = 16, color = "grey25") +
    geom_text(data = r2, aes(label = r2_label),
      x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.4,
      size = 3.5, color = "grey45", fontface = "italic", family = "noto") +
    scale_fill_manual(values  = c("Increasing" = col_inc, "Decreasing" = col_dec)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Increasing" = col_inc, "Decreasing" = col_dec)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2008, 2014, 2020)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = yaxis_labels[[param_name]], tag = letter) +
    theme_nature() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = if (show_xticks)
                      element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10)
                    else
                      element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x        = if (show_xticks) element_line() else element_blank(),
      axis.text.y         = element_text(size = 10, margin = margin(r = 1, unit = "pt")),
      axis.title.y        = element_text(margin = margin(r = 1, unit = "pt")),
      axis.ticks.length.y = unit(0.1, "cm"),
      plot.tag.position   = c(0.04, 0.96),
      plot.tag            = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, hjust = 0, vjust = 1),
      plot.margin         = margin(5, 5, 5, 2, unit = "pt")
    )
}

ts_panels_all <- pmap(
  list(param_levels, LETTERS[2:11], seq_along(param_levels) > 8),
  \(p, l, show) make_ts_panel(p, l, show_xticks = show)
)

# Equalize panel sizes by aligning left and right columns separately.
# align_plots(align = "v", axis = "l") pads the narrower y-axis areas within
# each column to match the widest, so all panels in a column have equal data-area
# widths. Columns are aligned independently to avoid over-padding.
left_aligned  <- cowplot::align_plots(
  plotlist = ts_panels_all[c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9)],  # B D F H J
  align = "v", axis = "l"
)
right_aligned <- cowplot::align_plots(
  plotlist = ts_panels_all[c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)],  # C E G I K
  align = "v", axis = "l"
)

all_aligned <- vector("list", 10)
all_aligned[c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9)]  <- left_aligned
all_aligned[c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)] <- right_aligned

panel_b <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = all_aligned, ncol = 2, align = "none")

# ── Combine and render ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Heights ratio 1:3.3 ≈ Panel A (~70 mm ridge) : Panel B (5 rows × ~46 mm)
fig7 <- panel_a / wrap_elements(panel_b) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 3.3)) &
  theme(plot.background = element_blank())

fig7

ggsave(
  here("Output", "fig7_temporal_trends.pdf"),
  plot   = fig7,
  width  = 183,
  height = 300,
  units  = "mm",
  device = cairo_pdf
)
```

**Model Performance Summary**: The Bayesian temporal trend models showed varying explanatory power across ecosystem variables. Herbivorous fish, N content, and coral cover trends had the highest R² values (>0.7), indicating highly predictable linear trajectories over time. Metabolic variables (Pmax, Rd, NP) showed moderate explanatory power (R² = 0.2-0.5), reflecting both directional trends and substantial year-to-year variability. 

### Temporal Rates of Change (Natural Scale)

```{r temporal-rate-table}
#| label: tbl-temporal-rates
#| cache: false
#| tbl-cap: "**Annual rates of change on the natural scale for each measured ecosystem parameter at MCR LTER Site 1 backreef, 2005–2025.** Rates are back-transformed from standardised Bayesian linear regression slopes (posterior median × variable SD). The 95% credible interval (CI) is derived from the 2.5th and 97.5th posterior quantiles. Direction indicates whether the trend is increasing or decreasing; credible trends have 95% CIs that exclude zero (†)."

# Units lookup (natural-scale units per year for each variable)
units_map_doc <- tibble(
  var   = c("mean_coral", "mean_fleshy", "Corallivore", "Herbivores",
            "N_percent", "Rd", "Pmax", "NP_mean", "Max_temp", "Nitrite_and_Nitrate"),
  Units = c("% cover yr\u207b\u00b9", "% cover yr\u207b\u00b9",
            "g m\u207b\u00b2 yr\u207b\u00b9", "g m\u207b\u00b2 yr\u207b\u00b9",
            "% N yr\u207b\u00b9",
            "mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 hr\u207b\u00b9 yr\u207b\u00b9",
            "mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 hr\u207b\u00b9 yr\u207b\u00b9",
            "mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 hr\u207b\u00b9 yr\u207b\u00b9",
            "\u00b0C yr\u207b\u00b9", "\u00b5mol L\u207b\u00b9 yr\u207b\u00b9")
)

# Summarise posterior slopes from temporal_results into median + 95% CI
slope_tbl_doc <- temporal_results |>
  group_by(Parameter) |>
  summarise(
    median_std = median(Year),
    lo95_std   = quantile(Year, 0.025),
    hi95_std   = quantile(Year, 0.975),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

slope_tbl_doc |>
  left_join(scale_params |> select(Parameter, sd, var), by = "Parameter") |>
  left_join(units_map_doc, by = "var") |>
  mutate(
    natural_slope = median_std * sd,
    natural_lo95  = lo95_std  * sd,
    natural_hi95  = hi95_std  * sd,
    credible      = sign(lo95_std) == sign(hi95_std),
    Rate = sprintf("%.3g (%s, %s)%s",
                   natural_slope,
                   formatC(natural_lo95, digits = 2, format = "g"),
                   formatC(natural_hi95, digits = 2, format = "g"),
                   if_else(credible, "\u2020", "")),
    Direction = if_else(median_std > 0, "\u2191 Increasing", "\u2193 Decreasing")
  ) |>
  arrange(median_std) |>
  select(Parameter, Units, `Rate (95% CI)` = Rate, Direction) |>
  kbl(align = c("l", "l", "r", "c")) |>
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width        = FALSE,
    position          = "left"
  ) |>
  footnote(
    general       = "\u2020 95% credible interval excludes zero.",
    general_title = ""
  )
```

## Correlation Analysis

```{r correlations}
#| label: fig-correlations
#| eval: false
#| include: false
#| fig-cap: "**Coral cover is strongly positively correlated with ecosystem respiration and corallivore biomass, and negatively correlated with temperature, fleshy macroalgae, and algal nitrogen.** Pairwise Pearson correlation matrix among ten reef ecosystem variables at MCR LTER Site 1 backreef, 2005–2025 (n = 15–21 annual observations per pair, depending on variable availability). Upper triangle: ellipses scaled and oriented by Pearson r; narrow horizontal ellipses indicate strong positive correlation, narrow vertical ellipses indicate strong negative correlation. Lower triangle: numeric r values. Variables are ordered by hierarchical clustering of the correlation matrix. Asterisks indicate significance from two-tailed t-tests: * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001 (no correction for multiple comparisons). NP = annual mean net community production (mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹); Rd = ecosystem dark respiration (mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹); Pmax = maximum photosynthetic capacity (mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹); %N = algal tissue nitrogen content (%); N+N = water-column nitrite + nitrate (µmol L⁻¹); % Coral = coral cover (%); % Algae = fleshy macroalgae cover (%); Herbs/eroder = herbivorous and bioeroding fish biomass (g m⁻²); Corallivore = corallivore fish biomass (g m⁻²); Max Temp = annual maximum sea surface temperature (°C)."
#| fig-width: 10
# Compute correlation matrix
ct <- corr.test(
  Year_Averages |>
    select(
      NP = NP_mean, Rd, Pmax, `%N` = N_percent,
      `N+N` = Nitrite_and_Nitrate, `% Coral` = mean_coral,
      `% Algae` = mean_fleshy, `Herbs/eroder` = Herbivores,
      `Corallivore` = Corallivore, `Max Temp` = Max_temp
    ),

)

corr <- ct$r
p.mat <- ct$p

ggcorrplot.mixed(corr,
  upper = "ellipse",

  insig = "label_sig",
  sig.lvl = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001)
```

## Structural Equation Modeling

Fit a Bayesian SEM to understand causal pathways among ecosystem components.

```{r sem-prep}
#| label: sem-preparation

# Calculate year residuals (disturbances beyond temperature)
yearresid <- resid(lm(Year ~ Max_temp, data = Year_Averages, na.action = na.exclude))

# Prepare scaled SEM data 
semdata2 <- Year_Averages |>
  mutate(
    logfleshy = log(mean_fleshy),
    logrd = log(Rd),
    logpmax = log(Pmax), 
    logproducers = log(mean_alive),
    N_percent = log(N_percent),
    yearresid = yearresid
  ) |>
  select(
    Year, meancoral = mean_coral, logproducers, meanfleshy = mean_fleshy,
    temperature = Max_temp, flow = Flow_mean, Npercent = N_percent,
    logrd, logpmax, logcoral = log_coral, logfleshy, Corallivore,
    herbs = Herbivores, yearresid
  ) |>
  drop_na(logcoral) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))
```

```{r sem-fit}
#| label: sem-model
#| cache: true

# Define SEM structure
bf_temp <- bf(temperature | mi() ~ 1 + Year)
bf_coraltemp <- bf(logcoral | trunc(ub = 3.39) ~ 1 + temperature + yearresid +
                     ar(time = Year, p = 1))
bf_logpmax <- bf(logpmax | mi() ~ 1 + logcoral + mi(temperature) + mi(logrd)) ####
bf_logrd <- bf(logrd | mi() ~ 1 + logcoral + mi(temperature))
bf_herbs <- bf(herbs | mi() ~ 1 + logfleshy)
bf_corallivore <- bf(Corallivore | mi() ~ 1 + logcoral)
bf_fleshy <- bf(logfleshy | trunc(ub = 2.26) ~ logcoral)
bf_nutrients <- bf(Npercent | mi() ~ 1 + mi(logrd))

# Fit full SEM
brms_sem_full <- brm(
  bf_temp + bf_coraltemp + bf_logrd + bf_herbs + bf_corallivore +
    bf_nutrients + bf_fleshy + bf_logpmax + set_rescor(FALSE),
  data = semdata2,
  chains = 3,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  seed = 11,
  sample_prior = "no",
  prior = c(
    set_prior("normal(0, 2)",    class = "b"),
    set_prior("normal(0, 2)",    class = "Intercept"),
    set_prior("normal(0, 0.25)", resp = "temperature", class = "sigma", lb = 0),
    set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)",  class = "ar",  resp = "logcoral")
  ),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15),
  family = gaussian(),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
)
```

```{r sem-summary}
#| label: sem-results

summary(brms_sem_full)
```

```{r}
#| label: sem-r2-calculation

# Calculate Bayesian R² for each response variable in the SEM
# Note: Some responses with missing data imputation may have NaN - filter these out
sem_r2 <- bayes_R2(brms_sem_full, summary = FALSE)
sem_r2_summary <- apply(sem_r2, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)

# Remove NaN values
sem_r2_valid <- sem_r2_summary[!is.na(sem_r2_summary)]

cat("\n=== Structural Equation Model: Bayesian R² by Response ===\n\n")
sem_r2_df <- tibble(
  Response = names(sem_r2_valid),
  R2 = sem_r2_valid
) |>
  mutate(Response = case_when(
    Response == "R2temperature" ~ "Temperature",
    Response == "R2logcoral" ~ "Coral Cover",
    Response == "R2logpmax" ~ "Ecosystem Pmax",
    Response == "R2logrd" ~ "Ecosystem Rd",
    Response == "R2herbs" ~ "Herbivorous Fish",
    Response == "R2Corallivore" ~ "Corallivore Fish",
    Response == "R2logfleshy" ~ "Fleshy Macroalgae",
    Response == "R2Npercent" ~ "N Content",
    TRUE ~ Response
  )) |>
  arrange(desc(R2))

print(sem_r2_df, n = Inf)

cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean R² across computable responses: %.3f\n", mean(sem_r2_valid)))
cat(sprintf("The SEM explains between %.1f%% and %.1f%% of variance across responses.\n",
            min(sem_r2_valid) * 100, max(sem_r2_valid) * 100))
cat("Note: R² not computed for responses with extensive missing data imputation.\n")
```

## SEM Conceptual Model

```{r sem-dag}
#| label: fig-sem-dag
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "**Temperature drives reef ecosystem degradation indirectly through coral loss, which propagates to all six downstream components across ecosystem function and community composition.** Directed acyclic graph (DAG) of the full Bayesian multivariate structural equation model (SEM) comprising 11 hypothesised causal pathways among nine ecosystem components, fit to n = 19 annual observations, 2006–2024 (MCR LTER Site 1 backreef). Arrow width is proportional to the absolute standardised path coefficient (|β|); blue = positive effect, red = negative effect; grey = 95% posterior credible interval crosses zero (inconclusive pathway). Standardised β values are shown on each arrow. Shaded regions distinguish ecosystem function variables (purple background; Ecosystem Respiration, Ecosystem Pmax, and Algal N Stock) from community composition variables (blue background; Fleshy Algae, Herbivore Fish, Corallivore Fish). All continuous variables were log-transformed where appropriate and z-score standardised (mean = 0, SD = 1) prior to analysis to permit direct comparison of effect magnitudes."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.2

pos_col  <- "#1565C0"
neg_col  <- "#B71C1C"
nsig_col <- "#AAAAAA"

# N Stock elevated above the Rd–Pmax horizontal line (y=5.0 vs Rd/Pmax at y=4.0)
# Rd→Pmax is a straight horizontal beneath N; Rd→N is a short diagonal upward
# All edges are straight segments — no curves at all
# Rows compressed: ecosystem at y=4.0, community at y=2.0, gap = 2.0 units
dag_nodes <- tribble(
  ~id,           ~label,                    ~x,    ~y,    ~fill,       ~border,
  "Year",        "Year",                    0.4,   3.5,   "white",     "#888888",
  "Temp",        "Temperature",             2.0,   3.0,   "white",     "#888888",
  "Coral",       "Coral\nCover",            3.8,   3.0,   "#E8F5E9",   "#2E7D32",
  # Ecosystem function: Rd and Pmax in horizontal row; N elevated above
  "Rd",          "Ecosystem\nRespiration",  5.6,   4.0,   "#EDE7F6",   "#4527A0",
  "N",           "N\nStock",               7.4,   5.0,   "#FFF8E1",   "#E65100",
  "Pmax",        "Ecosystem\nPmax",         9.2,   4.0,   "#EDE7F6",   "#4527A0",
  # Community composition row
  "Algae",       "Fleshy\nAlgae",           5.6,   2.0,   "#E8F5E9",   "#2E7D32",
  "Herbs",       "Herbivore\nFish",         7.4,   2.0,   "#E3F2FD",   "#0D47A1",
  "Corallivore", "Corallivore\nFish",       9.2,   2.0,   "#E3F2FD",   "#0D47A1"
)

dag_edges <- tribble(
  ~from,   ~to,           ~est,   ~sig,  ~loff_x, ~loff_y,
  "Year",  "Temp",        0.465,  TRUE,   0.28,    0.18,
  "Temp",  "Coral",      -0.546,  TRUE,   0.00,    0.24,
  "Temp",  "Rd",          0.214,  FALSE, -0.35,    0.24,
  "Temp",  "Pmax",       -0.158,  FALSE, -0.75,   -0.22,
  "Coral", "Rd",          1.077,  TRUE,  -0.08,    0.24,
  "Coral", "Algae",      -0.914,  TRUE,  -0.08,   -0.24,
  "Coral", "Corallivore", 0.644,  TRUE,   0.38,   -0.20,
  "Coral", "Pmax",       -0.353,  FALSE,  0.38,    0.20,
  "Rd",    "N",           0.620,  TRUE,  -0.18,    0.22,   # short diagonal up-right
  "Rd",    "Pmax",        0.820,  TRUE,   0.00,    0.24,   # straight horizontal below N
  "Algae", "Herbs",       0.710,  TRUE,   0.00,    0.24    # straight horizontal
) |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(est >= 0, "pos", "neg"), abs_est = abs(est)) |>
  left_join(dag_nodes |> select(id, x, y) |> rename(from = id, x0 = x, y0 = y), by = "from") |>
  left_join(dag_nodes |> select(id, x, y) |> rename(to   = id, x1 = x, y1 = y), by = "to") |>
  mutate(mx = (x0 + x1) / 2, my = (y0 + y1) / 2, lbl = sprintf("%.2f", est))

# All edges are straight — no geom_curve needed
dag_arr <- arrow(length = unit(3.0, "mm"), type = "closed")

ggplot() +
  # Faint region backgrounds
  annotate("rect", xmin = 4.8, xmax = 10.0, ymin = 3.2, ymax = 5.65,
           fill = "#EDE7F6", alpha = 0.18, color = NA) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 4.8, xmax = 10.0, ymin = 1.2, ymax = 2.75,
           fill = "#E3F2FD", alpha = 0.18, color = NA) +
  # Region labels
  annotate("text", x = 10.12, y = 4.5, label = "Ecosystem\nfunction",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.6, color = "#6A1B9A", fontface = "italic", lineheight = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 10.12, y = 2.0, label = "Community\ncomposition",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.6, color = "#1565C0", fontface = "italic", lineheight = 0.9) +
  # Significant edges
  geom_segment(data = filter(dag_edges,  sig),
    aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1, color = direction, linewidth = abs_est),
    alpha = 0.82, arrow = dag_arr, lineend = "butt") +
  # Non-significant edges — reduced alpha to de-emphasise
  geom_segment(data = filter(dag_edges, !sig),
    aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1, linewidth = abs_est),
    color = nsig_col, alpha = 0.45, arrow = dag_arr, lineend = "butt") +
  geom_label(data = filter(dag_edges,  sig),
    aes(x = mx + loff_x, y = my + loff_y, label = lbl, color = direction),
    size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", fill = "white",
    label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.07, "lines"), show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_label(data = filter(dag_edges, !sig),
    aes(x = mx + loff_x, y = my + loff_y, label = lbl),
    color = nsig_col, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", fill = "white",
    label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.07, "lines"), show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Node boxes
  {lapply(seq_len(nrow(dag_nodes)), function(i) {
    nd <- dag_nodes[i, ]
    geom_label(data = nd, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
               fill = nd$fill, color = nd$border, size = 3.0,
               fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.9, label.size = 0.65,
               label.padding = unit(0.38, "lines"), label.r = unit(4, "pt"),
               show.legend = FALSE)
  })} +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("pos" = pos_col, "neg" = neg_col),
                     labels = c("pos" = "Positive", "neg" = "Negative"),
                     name = "Effect direction") +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.6, 2.8), guide = "none") +
  labs(caption = "Standardized β on arrows  ·  gray = 95% CI crosses zero") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.caption    = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "grey55", size = 9, margin = margin(t = 6)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title    = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin     = margin(8, 10, 6, 10)
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.1, 11.8), ylim = c(1.35, 5.75))
```

## SEM Path Coefficients

```{r sem-paths}
#| label: fig-sem-paths
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "**Coral cover exerts the strongest and most consistent effects across the SEM, with large positive effects on ecosystem respiration (β = 0.96) and corallivore biomass (β = 0.64) and a large negative effect on fleshy macroalgae (β = −0.91).** Standardised path coefficients from the full Bayesian multivariate structural equation model (12 pathways; n = 15–21 annual observations per response variable, 2005–2025, MCR LTER Site 1 backreef). Each panel corresponds to one response variable; points show posterior medians and horizontal bars span 95% credible intervals derived from 15,000 post-warmup MCMC draws. Filled symbols (full opacity) indicate credible paths (95% CI excludes zero); faded symbols indicate inconclusive paths (CI crosses zero). All variables were log-transformed where appropriate and z-score standardised (mean = 0, SD = 1) prior to modelling, so β values are directly comparable across panels in units of standard deviations of the response per standard deviation of the predictor. Missing predictor values (temperature and ecosystem respiration as predictors of Pmax; ecosystem respiration as predictor of N content) were handled via integrated Bayesian imputation (*mi()* syntax in **brms**)."
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6

# Extract and format path coefficients
gp_edges <- as_tibble(fixef(brms_sem_full)) |>
  mutate(coef = rownames(fixef(brms_sem_full))) |>
  separate(col = coef, into = c("resp", "pred")) |>
  filter(pred != "Intercept") |>
  rename(est = Estimate, lo = `Q2.5`, hi = `Q97.5`) |>
  mutate(sig = if_else(sign(lo) == sign(hi), 1, 0.5)) |>
  mutate(resp = case_when(
    resp == "temperature" ~ "Temperature",
    resp == "logfleshy" ~ "Fleshy Macroalgae",
    resp == "logpmax" ~ "Ecosystem Pmax",
    resp == "logrd" ~ "Ecosystem Rd",
    resp == "herbs" ~ "Herbivorous Fish",
    resp == "Corallivore" ~ "Corallivore Fish",
    resp == "logcoral" ~ "Coral",
    resp == "Npercent" ~ "N stock"
  )) |>
  mutate(resp = factor(resp, c(
    "Temperature", "Coral", "Fleshy Macroalgae", "Herbivorous Fish",
    "Corallivore Fish", "Ecosystem Rd", "Ecosystem Pmax", "N stock"
  ))) |>
  mutate(pred = case_when(
    pred == "temperature" ~ "Temperature",
    pred == "mitemperature" ~ "Temperature",
    pred == "milogrd" ~ "Ecosystem Rd Rate",
    pred == "logcoral" ~ "Coral Cover",
    pred == "logfleshy" ~ "Fleshy Macroalgae Cover",
    pred == "Year" ~ "Year",
    pred == "yearresid" ~ "Non-Temperature Yearly Variability"
  )) |>
  mutate(pred = factor(pred, c(
    "Ecosystem Rd Rate", "Fleshy Macroalgae Cover",
    "Coral Cover", "Non-Temperature Yearly Variability",
    "Temperature", "Year"
  )))

gp_edges |>
  ggplot(aes(x = est, y = pred)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "firebrick", aes(alpha = sig)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, alpha = sig), height = 0, color = "firebrick") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  scale_alpha(range = c(0.4, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Standardized Effect Size",
    y = "Predictor Variables",
    title = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  facet_wrap(~resp, nrow = 1) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

ggsave(here("Output","Pathcoeffs.pdf"), width = 16, height = 6)
```

## Temperature Effects: Direct vs Indirect

```{r temp-effects-data}
#| label: temp-effects-data
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| cache: true

# ── Compute direct and indirect temperature effects from SEM posteriors ────────
# post_samples: 15,000 post-warmup draws from the full SEM
post_samples <- as_tibble(as.matrix(brms_sem_full))

# Individual path coefficient draws
b_tc  <- post_samples$b_logcoral_temperature       # Temp → Coral (direct)
b_cr  <- post_samples$b_logrd_logcoral             # Coral → Rd
b_cf  <- post_samples$b_logfleshy_logcoral         # Coral → Fleshy
b_cc  <- post_samples$b_Corallivore_logcoral       # Coral → Corallivore Fish
b_cp  <- post_samples$b_logpmax_logcoral           # Coral → Pmax
b_fh  <- post_samples$b_herbs_logfleshy            # Fleshy → Herbivore Fish
b_rn  <- post_samples$bsp_Npercent_milogrd         # Rd → N Content
b_tr  <- post_samples$bsp_logrd_mitemperature      # Temp → Rd (direct)
b_tp  <- post_samples$bsp_logpmax_mitemperature    # Temp → Pmax (direct)

n_draws <- nrow(post_samples)
zeros   <- rep(0, n_draws)

# Direct, indirect, and total effects for each response variable
effect_specs <- list(
  `Coral Cover`       = list(direct = b_tc,   indirect = zeros),
  `Ecosystem Rd`      = list(direct = b_tr,   indirect = b_tc * b_cr),
  `Fleshy Macroalgae` = list(direct = zeros,  indirect = b_tc * b_cf),
  `Corallivore Fish`  = list(direct = zeros,  indirect = b_tc * b_cc),
  `Ecosystem Pmax`    = list(direct = b_tp,   indirect = b_tc * b_cp),
  `Herbivore Fish`    = list(direct = zeros,  indirect = b_tc * b_cf * b_fh),
  `N Content`         = list(direct = zeros,  indirect = b_tc * b_cr * b_rn)
)

summarise_effect <- function(samps) {
  tibble(
    samples     = list(samps),
    median      = median(samps),
    lower       = quantile(samps, 0.025),
    upper       = quantile(samps, 0.975),
    significant = sign(quantile(samps, 0.025)) == sign(quantile(samps, 0.975))
  )
}

all_effects <- imap_dfr(effect_specs, function(spec, resp_name) {
  bind_rows(
    summarise_effect(spec$direct)               |> mutate(response = resp_name, effect_type = "Direct"),
    summarise_effect(spec$indirect)             |> mutate(response = resp_name, effect_type = "Indirect"),
    summarise_effect(spec$direct + spec$indirect) |> mutate(response = resp_name, effect_type = "Total")
  )
}) |>
  mutate(
    response    = factor(response,    levels = names(effect_specs)),
    effect_type = factor(effect_type, levels = c("Direct", "Indirect", "Total"))
  )
```

```{r temp-indirect-ranking}
#| label: fig-temp-indirect
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "**Temperature warming exerts its largest credible negative indirect effects on ecosystem respiration and corallivore biomass, and its largest credible positive indirect effect on herbivore biomass, all transmitted through coral cover loss.** Posterior median standardised indirect effects of annual maximum sea surface temperature on six ecosystem variables (n = 7 variables evaluated), transmitted exclusively through coral cover (β_indirect = β(Temperature→Coral) × β(Coral→Response)), derived from 15,000 post-warmup MCMC draws of the full Bayesian SEM (MCR LTER Site 1 backreef). Horizontal bars show posterior medians; error bars span 95% credible intervals. Blue = positive indirect effect (temperature → coral loss → increase in response); red = negative indirect effect (temperature → coral loss → decrease in response). Full opacity = credible effect (95% CI excludes zero); faded = inconclusive (CI crosses zero). Variables are ranked from most negative to most positive indirect effect. Effect sizes are in units of standard deviations of the response per standard deviation of temperature (all variables z-score standardised prior to modelling)."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

# Extract only indirect effects and rank them
indirect_effects <- all_effects |>
  filter(effect_type == "Indirect") |>
  # Remove coral (no indirect effect)
  filter(response != "Coral Cover") |>
  arrange(median) |>
  mutate(
    response = fct_reorder(response, median),
    direction = if_else(median < 0, "Negative", "Positive")
  )

# Create ranked bar plot
indirect_effects |>
  ggplot(aes(x = response, y = median, fill = direction, alpha = significant)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    width = 0.1,
    linewidth = 0.8,
    color = "gray20",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Negative" = "#E64B35", "Positive" = "#4DBBD5"),
    name = "Effect Direction"
  ) +
  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = 0.9, "FALSE" = 0.2),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Standardized Indirect Effect Size",
    #title = "Indirect Effects of Temperature via Coral Decline",
  #  subtitle = "Ranked from negative to positive effects with 95% credible intervals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 17, margin = margin(t = 10)),
   # legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.position = "none",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 19, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15, color = "gray40")
  )

ggsave(here("Output","Indirect.pdf"), width = 8, height = 6)
# Print ranked summary
cat("\n=== Ranked Indirect Effects (negative to positive) ===\n\n")
indirect_effects |>
  select(response, median, lower, upper, significant) |>
  mutate(across(median:upper, ~round(.x, 3))) |>
  arrange(median) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

## SEM Conditional Effects

```{r sem-conditional}
#| label: fig-sem-conditional
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "**All eight retained SEM causal pathways are strongly directional and ecologically interpretable, with temperature driving coral loss that cascades through ecosystem function and community composition.** Marginal posterior-predicted relationships for each significant predictor–response pair in the reduced Bayesian SEM (n = 15–21 annual observations per panel, 2005–2025, MCR LTER Site 1 backreef), with all other model predictors held at their posterior means. Lines show posterior medians; shaded ribbons show 95% credible intervals. Points are annual observed values back-transformed from z-score to measurement units. Panels are arranged in causal order from climate forcing through coral-mediated change to ecosystem function: (B) Year → Temperature, (C) Temperature → Coral Cover, (D) Coral Cover → Fleshy Algae, (E) Coral Cover → Ecosystem Respiration, (F) Coral Cover → Corallivore Fish, (G) Fleshy Algae → Herbivore Fish, (H) Ecosystem Respiration → Algal N Content, (I) Ecosystem Respiration → Ecosystem Pmax. Coral cover and fleshy algae axes are on log scales. Conditional effects were computed with `conditional_effects()` in **brms** and back-transformed using study-wide z-score parameters."
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 9.72

# Unscaling parameters
yearresid_full <- resid(lm(Year ~ Max_temp, data = Year_Averages, na.action = na.exclude))

Yearmodelvalues <- Year_Averages |>
  mutate(
    log_coral = log(mean_coral),
    logfleshy = log(mean_fleshy),
    logrd     = log(Rd),
    logpmax   = log(Pmax),
    N_percent = log(N_percent),
    yearresid = yearresid_full
  ) |>
  select(
    Year, meancoral = mean_coral, meanfleshy = mean_fleshy,
    temperature = Max_temp,
    Npercent = N_percent,
    logrd, logpmax, logcoral = log_coral,
    logfleshy, Corallivore, herbs = Herbivores, yearresid
  ) |>
  drop_na(logcoral)

modelmean <- Yearmodelvalues |> summarise(across(everything(), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
modelsd   <- Yearmodelvalues |> summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sd(x,   na.rm = TRUE)))

# ── Shared theme: 10 pt, exported at 183 × 247 mm ──────────────────────────
base_sz <- 10
rib_a   <- 0.25
rib_cl  <- "#67bed9"
ln_sz   <- 0.8
pt_sz   <- 1.8

theme_cond <- theme_classic(base_size = base_sz) +
  theme(
    plot.title   = element_text(size = base_sz, face = "bold"),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = base_sz),
    axis.text    = element_text(size = base_sz, color = "black"),
    axis.line    = element_line(linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.ticks   = element_line(linewidth = 0.4)
  )

# ── Row 1: Climate drivers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

temp_year <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "temperature", effects = "Year")
ty_plot <- as_tibble(temp_year$temperature.temperature_Year) |>
  mutate(
    Year       = Year       * modelsd$Year        + modelmean$Year,
    estimate__ = estimate__ * modelsd$temperature + modelmean$temperature,
    lower__    = lower__    * modelsd$temperature + modelmean$temperature,
    upper__    = upper__    * modelsd$temperature + modelmean$temperature
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = rib_a, fill = rib_cl) +
  geom_line(linewidth = ln_sz) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = Year, y = Max_temp), size = pt_sz, alpha = 0.55) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Temperature\n(\u00b0C)", title = "B  Year \u2192 Temperature") +
  theme_cond

coral_temp <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "logcoral", effects = "temperature")
ct_plot <- as_tibble(coral_temp$logcoral.logcoral_temperature) |>
  mutate(
    temperature = temperature * modelsd$temperature + modelmean$temperature,
    estimate__  = exp(estimate__ * modelsd$logcoral + modelmean$logcoral),
    lower__     = exp(lower__    * modelsd$logcoral + modelmean$logcoral),
    upper__     = exp(upper__    * modelsd$logcoral + modelmean$logcoral)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = temperature, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = rib_a, fill = rib_cl) +
  geom_line(linewidth = ln_sz) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = Max_temp, y = exp(log_coral)), size = pt_sz, alpha = 0.55) +
  coord_transform(y = "log") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 20, 40)) +
  labs(x = "Temperature\n(\u00b0C)", y = "Coral Cover\n(%)",
       title = "C  Temperature \u2192 Coral Cover") +
  theme_cond

# ── Row 2: Coral → benthos ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

fleshy_coral <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "logfleshy", effects = "logcoral")
fc_plot <- as_tibble(fleshy_coral$logfleshy.logfleshy_logcoral) |>
  mutate(
    logcoral   = exp(logcoral   * modelsd$logcoral  + modelmean$logcoral),
    estimate__ = exp(estimate__ * modelsd$logfleshy + modelmean$logfleshy),
    lower__    = exp(lower__    * modelsd$logfleshy + modelmean$logfleshy),
    upper__    = exp(upper__    * modelsd$logfleshy + modelmean$logfleshy)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = logcoral, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = rib_a, fill = rib_cl) +
  geom_line(linewidth = ln_sz) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = exp(log_coral), y = mean_fleshy), size = pt_sz, alpha = 0.55) +
  coord_transform(x = "log", y = "log") +
  labs(x = "Coral Cover\n(%)", y = "Fleshy Macroalgae Cover\n(%)",
       title = "D  Coral Cover \u2192 Fleshy Algae") +
  theme_cond

rd_coral <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "logrd", effects = "logcoral")
rc_plot <- as_tibble(rd_coral$logrd.logrd_logcoral) |>
  mutate(
    logcoral   = exp(logcoral   * modelsd$logcoral + modelmean$logcoral),
    estimate__ = exp(estimate__ * modelsd$logrd    + modelmean$logrd),
    lower__    = exp(lower__    * modelsd$logrd    + modelmean$logrd),
    upper__    = exp(upper__    * modelsd$logrd    + modelmean$logrd)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = logcoral, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = rib_a, fill = rib_cl) +
  geom_line(linewidth = ln_sz) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = exp(log_coral), y = Rd), size = pt_sz, alpha = 0.55) +
  coord_transform(x = "log", y = "log") +
  labs(
    x = "Coral Cover\n(%)",
    y = expression(atop("Ecosystem Respiration", "(mmol O"[2]*" m"^-2*" hr"^-1*")")),
    title = "E  Coral Cover \u2192 Respiration"
  ) +
  theme_cond

# ── Row 3: Coral → fish ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

corallivore_coral <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "Corallivore", effects = "logcoral")
cc_plot <- as_tibble(corallivore_coral$Corallivore.Corallivore_logcoral) |>
  mutate(
    logcoral   = exp(logcoral   * modelsd$logcoral    + modelmean$logcoral),
    estimate__ = estimate__     * modelsd$Corallivore + modelmean$Corallivore,
    lower__    = lower__        * modelsd$Corallivore + modelmean$Corallivore,

  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = logcoral, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = rib_a, fill = rib_cl) +
  geom_line(linewidth = ln_sz) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = exp(log_coral), y = Corallivore), size = pt_sz, alpha = 0.55) +

herbs_fleshy <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "herbs", effects = "logfleshy")
hf_plot <- as_tibble(herbs_fleshy$herbs.herbs_logfleshy) |>
  mutate(
    logfleshy  = exp(logfleshy  * modelsd$logfleshy + modelmean$logfleshy),

# ── Row 4: Metabolism → ecosystem function ─────────────────────────────────

N_Rd <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "Npercent", effects = "logrd")
nr_plot <- as_tibble(N_Rd$Npercent.Npercent_logrd) |>
  mutate(
    logrd      = exp(logrd      * modelsd$logrd    + modelmean$logrd),

# ── Assemble 4 × 2 grid and export at 183 × 247 mm ─────────────────────────
fig_cond <- (ty_plot | ct_plot) /
```
