## Supplementary Figure 1: Photosynthesis-Irradiance Curves

```{r fig-pi-curves}
#| label: fig-pi-curves
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "**Supplementary Figure 1. Both maximum photosynthetic capacity (Pmax) and ecosystem respiration (Rd) declined progressively from 2008 to 2025, consistent with the long-term loss of coral cover.** Annual photosynthesis–irradiance (PI) curves for MCR LTER Site 1 backreef. Points show individual hourly net community production measurements (n = 2,928 total; mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹) plotted against photosynthetically active radiation (PAR; µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹). Lines show the fitted rectangular hyperbola for each year, with parameters α (photosynthetic efficiency), Pmax (maximum photosynthetic capacity), and Rd (dark respiration) estimated simultaneously from all observations using the Bayesian non-linear model described in Methods (3 chains × 8,000 iterations, 2,000 warmup; Bayesian R² = 0.84). Inset text in each panel shows the posterior median Pmax and Rd (mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹)."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7

par_seq <- seq(0, max(LTER1_Pnet$PAR, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 200)

pi_params_plot <- fixef(fit1_f) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("param") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  separate(param, into = c("type", "year_str"), sep = "_Year", remove = FALSE) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year_str)) |>
  filter(!is.na(year)) |>
  select(type, year, Estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = Estimate) |>
  mutate(Rd = -Rd)

fitted_curves <- pi_params_plot |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(
    year   = year,
    PAR    = par_seq,
    PP_fit = (alpha * Pmax * par_seq) / (alpha * par_seq + Pmax) - Rd
  )

raw_data_plot <- LTER1_Pnet |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(as.character(Year)))

param_labels <- pi_params_plot |>
  mutate(
    label = sprintf("Pmax = %.0f\nRd = %.0f", Pmax, Rd),
    PAR   = max(LTER1_Pnet$PAR, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.97,
    PP    = min(LTER1_Pnet$PP,  na.rm = TRUE) * 0.85
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = raw_data_plot,
             aes(x = PAR, y = PP),
             colour = "grey50", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4, shape = 16) +
  geom_line(data = fitted_curves,
            aes(x = PAR, y = PP_fit),
            colour = "#1A237E", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = param_labels,
            aes(x = PAR, y = PP, label = label),
            hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 2.2, colour = "#1A237E",
            lineheight = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol = 6) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1000, 2000)) +
  labs(
    x = expression(PAR~(mu*mol~photons~m^{-2}~s^{-1})),
    y = expression(Net~production~(mmol~O[2]~m^{-2}~hr^{-1}))
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text       = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12)
  )

ggsave(here("Output","PICurves.pdf"), width = 9, height = 7)
```

## Supplementary Figure 2: SEM Observed vs. Fitted Trajectories

```{r fig-sem-obs-fit}
#| label: fig-sem-obs-fit
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "**Supplementary Figure 2. The reduced Bayesian SEM closely reproduces observed temporal trajectories for all eight ecosystem variables, supporting model adequacy.** Observed versus posterior-fitted annual trajectories for each sub-model of the reduced Bayesian SEM (MCR LTER Site 1 backreef, 2005–2025; n = 15–21 annual observations per sub-model depending on variable availability). Points show observed z-score standardised values; lines show the posterior median fitted value; shaded ribbons show the 95% credible interval from `fitted()` in **brms**. All variables are on the z-score scale used for model fitting. Missing observations (ecosystem respiration, Pmax, and N content in some years) are excluded from points but imputed internally by the model via Bayesian data augmentation. Sub-models are ordered by causal depth in the DAG."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

library(patchwork)

# Response metadata — ordered by causal depth in the DAG
resp_meta <- tibble(
  resp  = c("temperature", "logcoral", "logrd",  "logfleshy",
            "Corallivore", "herbs",    "logpmax", "Npercent"),
  label = c("Temperature", "Coral cover", "Ecosystem\nrespiration", "Fleshy\nmacroalgae",
            "Corallivore\nbiomass", "Herbivore\nbiomass", "Ecosystem\nPmax", "Algal N\ncontent")
)

# Actual calendar years aligned to semdata2 rows
# actual_years must match rows brms used: excludes years where any non-mi()
# predictor is NA (i.e. yearresid = NA when Max_temp = NA for 2025)
actual_years <- Year_Averages |>
  filter(!is.na(log_coral), !is.na(Max_temp)) |>
  pull(Year)

obs_fit_df <- resp_meta$resp |>
  map(function(r) {
    obs  <- semdata2[[r]]
    fit  <- fitted(brms_sem_reduced, resp = r)[, c("Estimate", "Q2.5", "Q97.5")]
    n_fit <- nrow(fit)
    tibble(
      Year     = actual_years[seq_len(n_fit)],
      observed = obs[seq_len(n_fit)],
      fitted   = fit[, "Estimate"],
      lo95     = fit[, "Q2.5"],
      hi95     = fit[, "Q97.5"],
      resp     = r
    )
  }) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  left_join(resp_meta, by = "resp") |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = resp_meta$label))

ggplot(obs_fit_df, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "#2c7bb6", alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fitted), colour = "#2c7bb6", linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(aes(y = observed), size = 1.6, colour = "black", na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2005, 2015, 2025), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "z-score") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
```

## Supplementary Figure 4: Bayesian R² by Sub-model

```{r fig-sem-r2}
#| label: fig-sem-r2
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "**Supplementary Figure 4. Sub-model explanatory power is high for temperature and coral cover (R² > 0.7) and moderate for metabolic and fish variables (R² = 0.4–0.7), supporting the adequacy of the causal DAG structure.** Bayesian R² for each sub-model of the reduced Bayesian SEM (MCR LTER Site 1 backreef, 2005–2025). Filled circles with bars show the posterior median R² and 95% credible interval, computed following Gelman et al. (2019) as Var(ŷ) / (Var(ŷ) + Var(ε)) across 500 posterior draws using `brms::bayes_R2()`. For sub-models with missing observations in the response variable (ecosystem respiration, corallivore biomass, herbivore biomass, ecosystem Pmax, and algal N content), `bayes_R2()` returns degenerate values because NAs propagate through the residual variance calculation; for these responses, the point estimate (open circle, no CI) is the squared Pearson correlation between posterior-mean fitted values and observed non-missing values. Sub-models are ordered by posterior median R²."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

# Always redefine resp_meta for this chunk to avoid inheriting factor levels
# or newline-embedded labels from fig-sem-obs-fit
resp_meta <- tibble(
  resp  = c("temperature", "logcoral", "logrd",  "logfleshy",
            "Corallivore", "herbs",    "logpmax", "Npercent"),
  label = c("Temperature", "Coral cover", "Ecosystem respiration", "Fleshy macroalgae",
            "Corallivore biomass", "Herbivore biomass", "Ecosystem Pmax", "Algal N content")
)

# Responses where bayes_R2 is reliable (no missing values in the response variable)
reliable_resps <- c("temperature", "logcoral", "logfleshy")
# Responses with missing values: bayes_R2 returns all-NA (NAs propagate through rowVars)
# Use squared correlation between posterior-mean fitted values and observed as fallback
manual_resps   <- c("logrd", "Corallivore", "herbs", "logpmax", "Npercent")

r2_reliable <- reliable_resps |>
  map(function(r) {
    draws <- as.vector(bayes_R2(brms_sem_reduced, resp = r, summary = FALSE, ndraws = 500))
    tibble(
      resp      = r,
      median_r2 = median(draws),
      lo95      = quantile(draws, 0.025),
      hi95      = quantile(draws, 0.975),
      method    = "bayes_R2"
    )
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

r2_manual <- manual_resps |>
  map(function(r) {
    obs      <- semdata2[[r]]
    fit_full <- fitted(brms_sem_reduced, resp = r)
    n_fit    <- nrow(fit_full)
    obs_fit  <- obs[seq_len(n_fit)]   # align to rows brms actually used
    ok       <- !is.na(obs_fit)
    fit      <- fit_full[ok, "Estimate"]
    tibble(
      resp      = r,
      median_r2 = cor(fit, obs_fit[ok])^2,
      lo95      = NA_real_,
      hi95      = NA_real_,
      method    = "manual"
    )
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

r2_df <- bind_rows(r2_reliable, r2_manual) |>
  left_join(resp_meta, by = "resp") |>
  arrange(median_r2) |>
  mutate(label = factor(as.character(label), levels = as.character(label)))

ggplot(r2_df, aes(x = median_r2, y = label)) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    data = filter(r2_df, method == "bayes_R2"),
    aes(xmin = lo95, xmax = hi95), height = 0.25, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = filter(r2_df, method == "bayes_R2"),
    size = 3, colour = "#2c7bb6"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = filter(r2_df, method == "manual"),
    size = 3, colour = "#2c7bb6", shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(x = expression(Bayesian~R^2), y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

## Supplementary Table 1: SEM Path Coefficients

```{r tbl-sem-paths}
#| label: tbl-sem-paths
#| tbl-cap: "**Supplementary Table 1.** Standardised path coefficients from the Bayesian multivariate structural equation model (12 pathways, n = 19 annual observations, 2006–2024). All continuous variables were log-transformed where appropriate and z-score standardised (mean = 0, SD = 1) prior to modelling. The coral sub-model includes a first-order autoregressive residual structure (AR(1)); the AR coefficient φ is reported as a separate row. Year residual is the residual of calendar year regressed on maximum annual temperature, capturing secular coral decline beyond the thermal trend. β = posterior median standardised path coefficient; 95% CI = posterior credible interval; Rhat = potential scale reduction factor (values < 1.01 indicate convergence); Bulk ESS = bulk effective sample size; Tail ESS = tail effective sample size. Pathways for which the 95% CI excludes zero are considered credible (marked †)."

# Build tidy table from brms fixed effects summary
sem_coef_table <- as.data.frame(summary(brms_sem_full)$fixed) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  # Keep only regression coefficients (exclude intercepts)
  filter(!grepl("Intercept", term)) |>
  mutate(
    # Parse response and predictor from "response_predictor" format
    Pathway = case_when(
      term == "temperature_Year"         ~ "Year → Temperature",
      term == "logcoral_temperature"     ~ "Temperature → Coral cover",
      term == "logcoral_yearresid"       ~ "Year residual → Coral cover",
      term == "logrd_logcoral"           ~ "Coral cover → Ecosystem respiration",
      term == "logrd_mitemperature"      ~ "Temperature → Ecosystem respiration (direct)",
      term == "logfleshy_logcoral"       ~ "Coral cover → Fleshy macroalgae",
      term == "Corallivore_logcoral"     ~ "Coral cover → Corallivore biomass",
      term == "herbs_logfleshy"          ~ "Fleshy macroalgae → Herbivore biomass",
      term == "logpmax_milogrd"          ~ "Ecosystem respiration → Ecosystem Pmax",
      term == "logpmax_logcoral"         ~ "Coral cover → Ecosystem Pmax (direct)",
      term == "logpmax_mitemperature"    ~ "Temperature → Ecosystem Pmax (direct)",
      term == "Npercent_milogrd"         ~ "Ecosystem respiration → Algal N content",
      TRUE ~ term
    ),
    Credible = if_else(sign(`l-95% CI`) == sign(`u-95% CI`), "†", ""),
    beta  = sprintf("%.3f", Estimate),
    CI    = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", `l-95% CI`, `u-95% CI`),
    Rhat  = sprintf("%.4f", Rhat),
    BESS  = formatC(round(Bulk_ESS), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
    TESS  = formatC(round(Tail_ESS), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
  ) |>
  # Order by causal chain
  mutate(order = case_when(
    grepl("Year →",              Pathway) ~ 1,
    grepl("Temperature →",       Pathway) ~ 2,
    grepl("Year residual →",     Pathway) ~ 2,
    grepl("Coral cover →",       Pathway) ~ 3,
    grepl("Fleshy macroalgae →", Pathway) ~ 4,
    grepl("Ecosystem respiration →", Pathway) ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ 6
  )) |>
  arrange(order, Pathway) |>
  select(Pathway, Credible, beta, CI, Rhat, `Bulk ESS` = BESS, `Tail ESS` = TESS)

kable(sem_coef_table, align = c("l", "c", "r", "c", "r", "r", "r"),
      col.names = c("Pathway", "", "β", "95% CI", "R̂", "Bulk ESS", "Tail ESS")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE,
                font_size = 12) |>
  column_spec(1, width = "14em") |>
  column_spec(2, width = "1em") |>
  footnote(symbol = "95% credible interval excludes zero.")
```

# Conclusions

This long-term analysis of Moorea's backreef ecosystem demonstrates the value of integrated, multi-decadal monitoring for understanding reef dynamics. The data reveal:

1.  **Clear directional change** in community composition driven primarily by warming
2.  **Complex feedbacks** among benthic communities, fish assemblages, and biogeochemical processes
3.  **Declining ecosystem function** as measured by net productivity and respiratory capacity
4.  **Predictable trajectories** that can inform management and restoration planning

Future research should focus on:

-   Identifying potential thresholds and tipping points in the transition process
-   Understanding resilience mechanisms and recovery potential
-   Evaluating management interventions to alter current trajectories
-   Exploring fine-scale spatial heterogeneity in ecosystem responses

The structural equation modeling approach employed here provides a framework for testing causal hypotheses and making projections, but predictions should be interpreted cautiously given the complexity of reef systems and potential for non-linear dynamics.
